dedupe_keys.name: national highway construction cost index nhcci fhwa

description: The National Highway Construction Cost Index (NHCCI) is a price index from the Federal Highway Administration that tracks price changes in highway construction costs and converts current-dollar spending on highway construction into real or constant dollars. It is intended to replace FHWA's older Bid-Price Index while allowing comparison with it over the historical period, and it is published quarterly together with the contributions of its components to quarterly changes. Coverage is national (United States). The index is free to view in an interactive dashboard and to download through its export function, with descriptions of the methods for the index and its component contributions, frequently asked questions and an analysis narrative; copies are deposited in research repositories such as openICPSR. Caveats: it is a single national index, and it measures construction prices, not maintenance or full life-cycle costs. The index supports economic parameters in highway investment appraisal, cost escalation in capacity planning and the costing of reconstruction after disasters. It complements the Highway Performance Monitoring System and is related to the ERA Railway System Data Inventory for rail costs.
